rationale:
The subject's obligations are covered by the marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]`.

- **Defaults from `TextQuery::new`:**
  - The test asserts the default `limit` is `None` and the default `context_lines` is zero.
  - The unscoped default query `^hit[0-9]$` returns all three matches from both `one.txt` and `two.txt`. That shows the default scope covers all files, and `complete` is true.
  - With zero context, every excerpt is exactly the four-character matching line, so "zero returns just the matching line" holds.
- **`pattern` is a regular expression:** `^hit[0-9]$` uses anchors and a character class. Only a regex engine would match the three hit lines and reject the middle line.
- **`scope` override:** `.scope(SourceScope::under("one.txt"))` restricts results to `one.txt` only. The expected entries are exactly the two `one.txt` matches, and the `two.txt` match is excluded.
- **`context_lines` override:**
  - `.context_lines(1)` gives the excerpt `hit1\nmiddle` for the first match (context after).
  - It gives `middle\nhit2` for the later match (context before).
  - Both sides are therefore exercised, and the reported line numbers are asserted too.
  - No single match has context on both sides at once. I did not count that as a gap, because the same input class (context of one, before and after) is checked on separate matches.
- **`limit` override and bounding across the scope:**
  - A limit of two over two files returns exactly two matches and `complete` is false. A per-file limit would have returned three, so the test rules that out.
  - A limit of one on the scoped query returns one match with `complete` false.
  - A limit that is not exceeded (two matches, limit two) gives `complete` true.
  - With no limit (`None`), all matches are returned.
- **Builder chaining:** `scoped.limit(1)` checks that a later builder call overrides an earlier value.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the exported inventory. It supports the struct and method declarations but adds no behavioral checks.

The word "visible" in "all visible files" appears to refer to the local-provider and `.gitignore` visibility rules. Those are governed by other requirements (`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider` and the source-scope requirement). I treated them as outside this subject. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: `TextQuery::new(pattern)` searches all visible files, with zero context lines and
no match limit. `scope`, `context_lines`, and `limit` override those defaults.

`pattern` is a regular expression. `context_lines` requests that many lines on either side of each matching line. Zero returns just the matching line. `limit` bounds matches across the scope. `None` requests all matches.
pub fn scope(self, scope: SourceScope) -> Self;
pub fn context_lines(self, context_lines: usize) -> Self;
pub fn limit(self, limit: usize) -> Self;
